title: Women’s Olympic events to be limited to biological females, IOC says
content:
The International Olympic Committee has announced compulsory gene testing to limit the women’s category of competition to biological females.

In an announcement on Thursday, the IOC said the new rule “protects fairness, safety and integrity in the female category” and does not apply to grassroots or recreational sports programmes. The testing, the IOC said, will see transgender women and some with differences in sexual development (DSD) barred from competing.

Athletes will have to undergo a one-time screening for the SRY gene, which is involved in male-typical sex development and is found on the Y chromosome.

The gene testing, described as “evidence‑based and expert‑informed” by the IOC, will come into effect for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games but will not be applied retroactively.

Thursday’s announcement follows the World Athletics ruling last July, which introduced the same requirement in time for the Tokyo World Championships that took place in September.

“As a former athlete, I passionately believe in the rights of all Olympians to take part in fair competition,” IOC president Kirsty Coventry said in a release on its website. “The policy that we have announced is based on science and has been led by medical experts.

“At the Olympic Games, even the smallest margins can be the difference between victory and defeat. So, it is absolutely clear that it would not be fair for biological males to compete in the female category. In addition, in some sports it would simply not be safe.”

More to follow.
